correctness.rationale: For m>=2, universal clique probes cannot monitor nonincident edges, while an independent probe has all clique vertices as first-layer neighbors and at least two possible predecessors for each distance-two independent vertex. Hence every probe monitors exactly its incident edges, making distance-edge-monitoring equivalent to vertex cover. The independent sets are exactly arbitrary subsets of the independent side and singleton clique vertices, yielding the enumerator and basis classification. For m=1, every edge is a bridge, so every nonempty set monitors all edges. Direct edge-deletion verification agrees for m,n=1..6.

value.rationale: The result gives a natural complete classification for a graph family whose minimum monitoring number has already attracted dedicated study. Knowing every monitoring set and the size enumerator measures redundancy and alternative sensor placements, information absent from the scalar optimum. The star-to-nonstar transition is structurally sharp and the closed form is reusable for reliability and counting questions.
